question: How do hyperscale software engineering factories (Google SRE, Google DeepMind, Microsoft Engineering, AWS Orchestration, OpenAI Frameworks, Anthropic MCP, Netflix Conductor, Palantir Foundry, SEI CMU, OWASP) achieve end-to-end mission proving, strategy deliberation, capability-driven tool routing, and independent meta-verification without vendor lock-in?
scope: End-to-end 25-step mission lifecycle integration, composition layer architecture, multi-agent council handoffs, failure recovery proving, and verifier independence
claims: End-to-end mission proving requires a composition layer that orchestrates existing specialized engines without duplicating state machines or policy logic.
Verifier independence is essential to prevent self-certification loops where execution actors approve unverified outputs.
evidence: AWS Step Functions and Netflix Conductor use top-level state machine orchestrators to compose granular sub-workflows and microservices.
SEI CMU software factory standards require traceable evidence chains for every artifact before release sign-off.
observations: Structured context handoffs between Agent Council roles require explicit facts, assumptions, artifacts, and verification criteria.
Controlled failure injection during mission proving proves that retries, fallbacks, replans, and rollbacks operate within policy bounds.
limitations: Mission proving operates via synthetic mock adapters prior to live commercial API activation.
recommendation: Implement Autonomous Engineering Factory Integration Engine, End-to-End Mission Contracts, Proving Scorecard Engine, and Meta-Verification auditing in EOS Control Plane.
